input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are not more common or always unsurvivable because modern buildings are built with strict fire safety regulations. These include fire-resistant materials, multiple escape routes, smoke detectors, sprinkler systems, and clearly marked exits. Buildings also have fire alarms that alert everyone quickly, and elevators are designed to help people evacuate safely during a fire. Because of these safety measures, most high-rise office fires can be controlled or people can escape before being harmed.
